title: Core of the Truehearted 4
content:
Wei Wuxian spun on his heel and sprinted toward the Blood Pool, Lan Wangji matching him stride for stride. The blood-red Spirit-Attraction Flag painted across his chest worked like a charm—every single corpse ignored the fleeing cultivators, brushing past living bodies without a second glance. Eyes gleaming a manic, hungry scarlet, the entire horde zeroed in on Wei Wuxian alone.

They came on in an endless, relentless tide. The narrow escape route Wen Ning carved through the crush was instantly swallowed by fresh corpses, forcing him to circle back and smash through the line again and again. More than half the cultivators in the cave were still scrambling to get out, several unable to even drag themselves across the floor. Behind them, Bichen’s sword-glare flashed with clinical, dazzling fury, butchering one rank of the dead into severed limbs only for the next to surge into the meat grinder. Bone-chilling shrieks and dying groans echoed off the cavern walls, loud enough to shake the subterranean vault to its foundation.

Before long, the sea of corpses had walled Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji into an iron ring, cutting them off from the Blood Pool entirely. The mound of rotting bodies around them grew higher by the second, tightening the perimeter until there was barely room to breathe.

Seeing the two trapped, the juniors lost what little composure they had left. Drawing steel, they broke rank and charged back into the fray.

Lan Jingyi grabbed at a cultivator who was slashing his way toward the exit. "Can you lend a hand?! If you can still hold a sword, get in there and help! Any little bit helps, come on!"

The man snarled, "Get the hell out of my face!"

Lan Sizhui caught Jingyi's shoulder. "Forget it, Jingyi! We do this ourselves!"

Hearing their voices over the din, Wei Wuxian bellowed across the hall: "Wen Ning! Throw them out! All of them!"

"On it!" Wen Ning grabbed Lan Jingyi by the collar with one hand and reached for Lan Sizhui with the other.

Sizhui planted his feet, shouting right into the Ghost General's face: "Ghost General, I can't leave! You have to let me stay! If I run now, I'll regret it for the rest of my life!"

Locked eye-to-eye with the boy, Wen Ning froze, his hand hanging motionless in midair. Seeing his chance, Sizhui slipped past him and charged into the slaughter, blade raised. Lan Jingyi and the other disciples took the cue, ducking past Wen Ning to rejoin the fight.

Further down the line, Jiang Cheng was half-dragging, half-hauling Jin Ling toward the cave mouth, brushing past a dozen snarling corpses. Pinned beneath the magnetic pull of the Spirit-Attraction Flag, the ghouls kept their feral stares locked on Wei Wuxian, completely blind to the living slipping past their flanks.

Jin Ling yelled over the noise, "Jiujiu! I..."

Jiang Cheng’s voice was arctic: "You take one step back in there, and you're no nephew of mine!"

Jin Ling stared at him, stunned. Jiang Cheng shove him roughly toward the daylight. "Stay put!"

Spinning on his heel, Jiang Cheng gripped Sandu and charged right back into the belly of the Demon-Subduing Cave.

Jin Ling froze for a split second, then scrambled after him. "Jiujiu, wait for me!"

Inside, the pocket around Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji had shrunk to less than ten feet across.

Bichen’s blade-glare remained pristine, and bursts of talisman fire continued to detonate in blinding flashes, but the numbers were simply too overwhelming.

Wei Wuxian hurled another handful of charms, only for his instincts to flare with cold dread. Glancing sideways, a corpse had scrambled to the top of a man-sized pile of dead flesh, snapping its jaw as it lunged straight for his throat. His hands were empty. Cursing, he dove into his sleeves for another talisman—and came up with nothing.

His stomach dropped through the floor.

He had burned through his entire stash.

Lan Wangji caught the opening from the corner of his eye, whipping Bichen around to parry—only for a piercing shriek to rip through the air as the leaping corpse tore clean in two mid-flight.

No. It hadn't split. It had been ripped apart with bare hands.

And whatever had shredded it was towering right before their eyes.

Perched atop the mountain of severed corpses was a ghoul drenched in dripping, scarlet gore. In each fist, it dragged half of the twitching, dismantled body, its eyeless face tilted down to gaze at Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji.

Lan Jingyi’s jaw hit the flagstones. Ouyang Zizhen breathed, "...Ancestors preserve us... what the hell is that?"

Everyone who laid eyes on the nightmare shared the exact same thought: What in the gods' names is that thing?!

It looked like nothing they had ever encountered. From its scalp to its boots, it was coated in a thick, dripping layer of fresh crimson, looking as though it had just dragged itself out from the bottom of the Blood Pool. Gaunt, skeletal, and horrifyingly vicious.

Even the horde bound to the Yin Tiger Tally paused, their attention snagged by this grotesque arrival. Abandoning their assault on Wei Wuxian, they hovered in place, staring toward the crest of the corpse pile in eerie hesitation.

The blood corpse took two staggering steps forward.

As it lurched down the mound, its joints popped with a sharp, sickening rattle, almost like a man rolling his shoulders to stretch. Thick, dark blood dripped steadily from its limbs and torso, leaving a slick, crimson trail in the dirt.

A suffocating aura of rancid, feral resentment radiated from its frame in waves. As it crept closer, the surrounding fierce corpses began shuffling backward, hissing in instinctual dread. The living cultivators went pale as chalk, paralyzed with held breath.

Lan Wangji stepped forward, positioning his body between the creature and Wei Wuxian. But Wei Wuxian reached out, his hand pressing down on Lan Wangji’s sword-arm, murmuring: "...Wait."

His eyes were glued to the blood corpse, a wild, impossible suspicion detonating behind his ribs, his heart hammering against his chest.

"Wait," he repeated, barely a whisper.

The creature halted about ten paces away. Tilting its chin toward the vaulted stone ceiling, it let loose two ear-splitting screeches.

The shrieks were sharp as broken glass, driving everyone to clamp their hands over their ears.

Far across the cavern, the surface of the Blood Pool rippled.

At first, it looked like a pebble had disturbed the dark mirror. But the ripples expanded into violent waves, churning the viscous, iron-thick liquid from below.

Splash.

A hand erupted through the gore.

The fingers clamped onto the rocky ledge, digging deep into the stone. Breaking the surface right behind it was a half-rotted, featureless face coated in dripping red.

A second blood corpse dragged itself out of the pool.

Within seconds, the entire basin began to froth and heave like a boiling cauldron. Thick, wet bubbles popped across the surface as more heads broke through. A third. A fourth. A fifth...

Each one crawled from the depths drenched in blood, faces twisted in grotesque snarls, screeching into the dark. And the second their feet hit solid ground, they threw themselves headlong into the advancing horde!

The army chained to the Yin Tiger Tally was hit like a wave breaking against a jagged reef. The blood corpses tore through their ranks like crimson cleavers, reducing the dead to a storm of shredded meat, splintered bone, and black gore!

Jin Ling choked on his breath. "...What are these things?! Why are there still corpses in the Blood Pool?! I thought every single fierce corpse on this mountain was burned to ash thirteen years ago?!"

Shielding his son, Sect Leader Ouyang blurted out, "Not all of them!"

Lan Jingyi yelled, "Which ones weren't?!"

"The... the ones..."

The words caught in his throat. He couldn't bring himself to say it. Thirteen years ago, after the crusade butchered the fifty-odd Wen remnants holed up on the mountain... their bodies had all been dumped into the Blood Pool.

"Watch out!" Jin Ling screamed.

A scarlet silhouette came crashing down right before them. Lan Sizhui raised his blade, scrambling back two paces as the blood corpse hauled itself upright.

It was an exceptionally frail, hunched creature. Its skull bore a jagged, hollow fracture, and a few strands of thinning white hair clung damply to its scalp, soaked in drying gore. Combined with the half-decayed flesh sloughing off its bones, it was a nauseating, terrifying sight. Dragging one twisted foot behind the other, it slowly limped toward Lan Sizhui. The surrounding juniors broke into a cold sweat, closing ranks with drawn swords.

Cornered by living breath, the corpse grew instantly guarded, a low hiss scraping in its throat. The boys tensed, bracing for the lunge, but Lan Sizhui held up a hand. "Don't move!"

His pulse was racing, yet deep down, an inexplicable calm held him steady. He wasn't afraid.

If the creature had pupils, it was staring straight at him. Tilting its crooked neck, it slowly lifted a trembling, withered arm toward Lan Sizhui, as if reaching out to touch his cheek.

The hand was caked in grime and blood, twisted and claw-like, sending a violent shiver down the spines of the young cultivators. Jin Ling raised Suihua to cut the arm down, but Sizhui blurted out, "Young Master Jin, don't!"

Jin Ling snapped, "Then what are we supposed to do?!"

"Just... don't move. Nobody move."

The blood corpse let out a soft, reedy wheeze. Steadying his breath, Lan Sizhui slowly reached his own hand out to meet it.

Just as their fingers were about to brush, another cluster of hostile corpses charged the flank. The blood corpse whipped around with a furious howl, launching itself into the fray. It tore into the ranks with feral, manic ferocity—shredding limbs, snapping necks, and painting the stone in gore. The deafening roar and the savage, blinding speed of its attacks stood in jarring, impossible contrast to the fragile hesitation it had shown a second before.

Wen Ning threw several corpses aside, his frame shaking violently as he screamed toward the scarlet figure: "Is that you?!"

The corpse didn't answer.

All around them, the red phantoms threw themselves into the slaughter. Wen Ning cried out, his voice cracking: "Is it you guys?!"

The cavern rang with shrill, chaotic screeches. Not a single soul answered him. None of them had the breath to answer.

Within half an hour, the din of slaughter finally began to fade.

When the dust settled, the Demon-Subduing Cave was indistinguishable from a painting of the underworld.

The surviving blood corpses slowly began drifting toward Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji.

Tall and short, men and women, young and old—every single one was a walking nightmare bathed in gore. Yet looking upon those broken silhouettes, Wei Wuxian caught glimpses of faces he had known.

Wen Ning murmured in a broken daze: "Fourth Uncle..."

"...Granny..."

He whispered the names one by one, his voice trembling harder with every syllable.

"Have you... been waiting here the entire time?"

If his dead eyes could still cry, they would have been burning red, flooded with tears.

Wei Wuxian’s lips parted, desperate to say something, anything. Yet the words withered on his tongue.

Lowering his head, he dropped into a deep, solemn bow, his voice thick and rough: "...Thank you."

Beside him, Lan Wangji bowed in identical, quiet reverence.

The creatures that had butchered their way through a horde with savage brutality stood facing the two men. Their faces remained horrifying masks of death, yet their movements turned clumsy, hesitant. One by one, in a jagged, uneven wave, they raised their blood-soaked hands and bowed in return.

And then, as if whatever phantom spark had animated them was suddenly snuffed out, they collapsed.

Their scarlet frames shattered like brittle porcelain, spider-webbing into dust, grinding smaller and smaller against the stone floor. It felt as though a single passing breeze would scatter every trace of them into thin air.

Wen Ning dropped to his knees, his hands frantically scooping the red ash together. He gathered fistfuls of the dust, shoving it desperately into his robes until his inner layers were bulging.

Seeing him scramble, Lan Jingyi scratched his head, unclasped his embroidered sachet, dumped the dried herbs onto the dirt, and knelt beside him. "Here!"

The other boys quickly followed suit, unhooking their pouches and sachets. Only Jin Ling hung back, looking between the boys and Wen Ning with an unreadable, guarded grimace before drifting quietly away. Pinned beneath half a dozen outstretched hands offering empty pouches, Wen Ning blinked, utterly at a loss.

Lan Sizhui asked gently, "Ghost General, do you need a hand?"

"No, you... you shouldn't—"

Lan Jingyi grumbled, "Look at this pile of ash! You think you can shovel all that up alone?!"

Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji walked over. "Don't touch it with your bare hands. Without gloves, you'll catch corpse poisoning."

The boys drew their hands back.

Lan Sizhui bowed. "Senior Wei, Hanguang-jun, Ghost General... thank you for saving us—"

A cold, venomous voice cut through the cavern: "Thank them for what?"

The juniors turned. Pushing his way to the front was Fang Mengchen.

The young cultivator glared with raw, burning fury. "What the hell was that supposed to be?!"

Lan Sizhui blinked, lost. "What do you mean?"

Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji turned their eyes on him.

Fang Mengchen spat, "I asked you: what was that farce?! A performance to balance his sins?! Don't tell me you idiots are actually feeling grateful to him right now?!"

A heavy, dead silence descended on the Demon-Subduing Cave. Not even a whisper dared break the gloom.

Truth be told, everyone in the room felt an ugly, bitter taste in their mouths.

They had marched up the mountain in glorious, unified righteous fervor to exterminate a monster, only to get hunted like stray dogs. And in the end, they had to rely on the very "monster" they came to butcher just to keep their heads attached.

Was it ridiculous? Surreal? Mortifying? Absurd?

Standing there after spending the afternoon howling for blood, nobody felt particularly dignified.

Thanking Wei Wuxian felt like swallowing glass; but having literally just been pulled from the jaws of death by his hand, claiming they owed him nothing felt equally monstrous. Under the circumstances, keeping their mouths shut was the only face-saving move left on the board.

Met with absolute silence, Fang Mengchen’s temper exploded.

He drew his blade, pointing the steel straight at Wei Wuxian's throat. "Putting on a little show of repentance—does that wipe the blood off your hands?! Does that erase the mountain of corpses you've piled up?!"

Wei Wuxian sidestepped the point. A few cultivators tried to play peacemaker: "Brother Fang! Calm down, let it go..."

The second the words cleared his mouth, the man realized his mistake. Fang Mengchen’s eyes burned scarlet. "Let it go?! What do you mean let it go?! He slaughtered my parents, and you want me to just let it go?!"

His voice cracked into a frantic roar: "Wei Wuxian murdered my mother and father! That is a stone-cold fact! So why the hell is he standing here looking like some righteous hero?! He does one good deed and the world completely forgets what he is?! Then what were my parents' lives to him?!"

In the crowd, Jin Ling’s fists clenched tight. Suddenly, a dull, crushing grip clamped down onto his shoulder—Jiang Cheng’s fingers digging into his muscle like iron talons.

Jin Ling couldn't see his uncle's face. He whispered, "...Jiujiu?"

A low, unreadable scoff scraped from Jiang Cheng’s throat.

Wei Wuxian finally spoke. His tone was dead even.

"Then what do you want?"

Fang Mengchen froze.

Wei Wuxian stepped forward. "Tell me: what do you actually want from me? You want to see me torn apart, broken and bleeding, just to soothe the poison rotting in your chest, don't you?"

He pointed back toward the unconscious Yi Weichun. "He lost a leg; I was ripped to shreds by my own corpses. You lost your parents; my entire family was wiped out down to the roots. I was cast out like a mangy dog, and I never even got to see my parents' ashes."

He turned back to the crowd. "Or is it the Wen remnants you hate? The 'Wen scum' you love to spit on died thirteen years ago. And right here, not ten minutes ago, they threw themselves into the meat grinder for my sake—and to save your miserable lives. They died for you a second time. And this time, their souls were burned to nothing."

He took another step, his gaze cutting like a blade. "So tell me: what else do you want?!"

Fang Mengchen glared back, teeth grinding until bone creaked. "It doesn't matter. Let me tell you something, Wei Wuxian: no matter what tricks you pull, don't you dare think I will ever forgive you! I will never forget what you did to my parents!" He screamed at the top of his lungs, "never!"

Wei Wuxian looked him dead in the eye. "Nobody asked for your forgiveness. The things I did—you remember them, and so do I. You won't forget? Good. Because I won't forget either."

Locked in that suffocating glare, Fang Mengchen felt an overwhelming, hollow despair cave in his ribs.

His life had undeniably been saved by Wei Wuxian and his dead retainers, yet laying down his blood feud was impossible. But seeking revenge on his own was pure suicide. In the end, he let out an agonizing, broken yell, spun on his heel, and sprinted blindly out of the cave.

The moment his footsteps vanished into the night, a voice chimed in from the back: "There... aren't any more corpses coming, right? We're actually safe this time, aren't we?!"

Hearing that voice, everyone felt a collective migraine coming on. Him again!

Nie Huaisang peeked around the room. Seeing no one answering, he shrank back, timidly offering: "So... can we leave now?"

For once, the man had asked the million-dollar question. Every single soul in the cavern was desperate to mount their swords and fly back to their ancestral halls as fast as the winds could carry them.

A female cultivator broke the silence: "Four hours should be just about up. How much spiritual energy has everyone recovered?"
